title: Anonymous Auction Protocol Based on Time-Released Encryption Atop Consortium BlockChain
central_claims: Under an honest time server and secure underlying primitives, timed-release encryption prevents early bid disclosure and auctioneer-bidder collusion.
Blind signatures and one-time addresses provide bidder anonymity, one bid per identity, and public result verification.
Off-chain cryptographic computation keeps the Ethereum auction protocol efficient and feasible.

source_manifest.title: Anonymous Auction Protocol Based on Time-Released Encryption Atop Consortium BlockChain
source_manifest.finding: Proposes timed-release auction with an honest time server; evaluates off-chain primitives and Ethereum feasibility.

source_manifest.title: Riggs: Decentralized Sealed-Bid Auctions
source_manifest.finding: Explicitly contrasts Xiong–Wang’s trusted time-server construction with computational timed commitments; this is a trust-model comparison, not a broken-security result.

source_manifest.title: Integration of Blockchain and Auction Models: A Survey, Some Applications, and Challenges

source_manifest.finding: Discusses the earlier timed-auction line in related work; its own construction addresses privacy after auctions and does not implement the assigned protocol.

search_gaps: Full original, Riggs related-work/security-model discussion, survey context and Cryptobazaar related-work discussion were read. No independent experimental reproduction or operational implementation was located.
No empirical security failure is inferred solely from the trusted time-server limitation, which the original states explicitly.
research.summary: Independent later work uses the protocol as a concrete trust-model comparator. Its honest time-server requirement remains explicit; replication, deployment, and retention of its claimed efficiency remain unverified.
